I’ve been farming these 13 mu for 30 years, and my father did before me. Around here in Quzhou, the land is good but you have to work it right. I plant winter wheat in October after rotary tilling the maize stubble, and then the minute the wheat comes off in early June, I put in the summer maize. That’s the system that feeds two of us. I use improved wheat seed from the county supply store — it’s reliable and not too expensive — and hybrid maize seed, always hybrid. For fertilizer, I spread about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu on the wheat, plus some phosphorus and potash, because the soil needs feeding after the maize. For maize I put down about 15 kg of nitrogen, and some P and K. I irrigate the wheat three times: before winter, at jointing, and at heading. The well gives me water, but pumping costs money so I don’t waste it. The maize gets two irrigations if the summer turns dry. I spray twice on each crop — herbicide first, then once more for insects or mildew if they show up. For maize I plant straight into the wheat stubble with no tillage; saves me and my wife precious days when the weather window is tight. I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and 550 kg per mu from the maize. At 55, I don’t chase miracles. I chase a reliable harvest that pays for the inputs and leaves a little aside.
